mechanism: Four-domain cone USDX→EURUSD/USDJPY→EURJPY; each domain holds autocorrelation of last-N vs prior-N weekly closes for Fibonacci N∈{3,5,8,13,21} (or RSI-mapped denser buckets under monomorphism); product domain uses geometric mean of shifted correlations (+1,√,−1); pick USDX period with highest corr as shared N and compare geometric mean to realized EURJPY corr.
data_needed: Weekly closes for USDX, EURUSD, USDJPY, EURJPY; correlation over paired N-bar windows; optional RSI for injective period remapping; 6-month walk of cones.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDX-JUN23, EURUSD, USDJPY, EURJPY; weekly (W1); 2021-07-01 to 2022-01-01.
why_new_for_mis: Cross-pair, multi-horizon autocorrelation cone that selects lookback from dollar-index self-similarity—MIS can sense when FX cross correlations cohere across Fibonacci horizons rather than a single fixed window.
quote: the domains each contain correlations across the periods 3,5,8,13, & 21 and the homomorphisms f, g, f’, and g’, will simply pair these across the domains by these periods.

mechanism: Coproduct cone: Bollinger envelope range (upper−lower) as apex factors, baseline MA as push-out; select N∈{3..21} by minimum baseline MA std-dev (or surjective cardinality under epimorphism); compare envelope delta to next-bar actual high-low range; epimorphic domain expansion lifts correlation of forecast vs actual from ~0.12 to ~0.16.
data_needed: Bid/close series; multi-period Bollinger upper/lower/baseline MA; per-period std-dev for N selection; actual bar range.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDX-JUN23 weekly; periods 3,5,8,13,21 (and 3–21 dense under epi).
why_new_for_mis: Volatility sensor that treats BB width as a category-theoretic envelope forecast gated by quietest baseline—MIS range expectation without raw ATR alone.
quote: The difference (or ‘coproduct union’) between these two will provide our forecast for the Bollinger Envelope range.

mechanism: Spearman corr of recent closes vs lagged lows (long index) and vs lagged highs (short index); bucket into 0..5 by golden-ratio thresholds; each index selects a partial-order (two of lookback/applied-price/indicator; third undefined) or linear-order (all three comparable) decision path for trailing-stop monoid steps.
data_needed: Close/high/low buffers over Lookback; MathCorrelationSpearman; monoid sets for lookback, applied price, indicator; Awesome Oscillator signal + fixed margin.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDJPY; past 12 months; trailing on AO library signal.
why_new_for_mis: Path-shape autocorrelation becomes an explicit discrete regime index that rewrites which intermediate trade decisions are comparable—MIS structure sensor beyond a single indicator reading.

mechanism: Four monoids (timeframe, lookback, applied price, RSI/BB indicator 0–100) produce regularized inputs to a single-hidden-layer MLP trained bar-by-bar to forecast ideal stop-loss gap; lot size = (m_percent·free_margin) / ((gap/tick_size)·tick_value); objects vs morphisms functors compared vs fixed-margin control.
data_needed: OHLC; monoid set cardinalities/identity/ops; MLP weights (file load/save); RSI signal class; free margin and tick metrics.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: BTCUSD daily; 2020-01-01 to 2023-08-01; RSI entry, no trailing.
why_new_for_mis: Sequence of discrete trade-decision monoids as the feature front-end to a neural stop-distance sensor—MIS can sense expected adverse excursion conditioned on selected TF/lookback/price/indicator state.
quote: The target output for which our MLP will be trained will be the ideal stop loss points for an open position. The size of this stop loss gap is inversely proportional to the lots traded

mechanism: Domain: USDJPY close-change series; codomain: EURJPY and EURUSD series; four RDFs map square corners AB/AC/BD/CD; induction lag n collapses n commuting squares into one rectangle so forecasts target EURUSD change n bars ahead; emit only when ABD and ACD agree on sign; score strict/generic directional match vs misses.
data_needed: Close changes for USDJPY, EURJPY, EURUSD; training/test date split; n_inductions; Alglib DFBuildRandomDecisionForest trees and R.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDJPY.ln, EURJPY, EURUSD; daily (D1); induction lags 1–8 logged.
why_new_for_mis: Triangular-arbitrage-linked multi-horizon change sensor with commute agreement gate—MIS cross-pair directional forecast at tunable bar lag without separate models per horizon.
quote: Induction allows us to look at these forecasts across multiple bars, as opposed to just one as we had in the last article.

mechanism: Last 4 close-to-close changes + 4-wave sine positional encoding (× point size); decode-only stack: MLP query/key/value → causal self-attention (token vs self and earlier tokens) → SoftMax weights × values → feed-forward; trains bar-by-bar as wizard signal class.
data_needed: Sequential close changes; positional sine coords; MLP weights for Q/K/V and FF; SoftMax; optional multi-decoder stacks (__DECODERS).
why_new_for_mis: Causal self-attention over lagged price-change tokens as an explicit relative-importance sequence sensor—MIS can weight which past bars matter now without RNN recurrence.
quote: What this does is compute the relative importance of each word in a sentence to words that appear before it in that sentence.

mechanism: Compound object: N lagged closes; simple object: MA of length N staggered N bars ahead; Fisher LDA (3 classes: bearish=0, whipsaw=1 if |ΔMA|≤regularizer·point, bullish=2) maps lagging prices to future MA change; unknown centroid nearest-class → signal direction.
data_needed: Close series; m_independent (=MA period); m_data training rows; m_regularizer; Alglib FisherLDAN weight matrix.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GBPUSD; 2023 start→June backtest, walk to August.
why_new_for_mis: Natural-transformation framing of lagged raw prices vs future smoother as an LDA regime classifier with explicit white-noise deadband—MIS bull/flat/bear sensor at MA horizon.
quote: we will use a method we are yet to consider in these series and that is the linear discriminant analysis (LDA).

mechanism: Three functors A/B/C = MAs of increasing periods on raw closes; natural transforms AB=A−B and BC=B−C logged in rolling buffers; Spearman correlation of the two NT buffers >0 confirms sum of MA increments as trend (else whipsaw filter); used as wizard signal.
data_needed: Close series; m_functor_a/b/c periods; m_transformations buffer length; MathCorrelationSpearman.
why_new_for_mis: Correlation of multi-speed MA-spread series as a meta-regime filter on whether MA trend increments are trustworthy—MIS trend-vs-chop sensor built from vertical natural transforms.
quote: A positive value should indicate the markets are trending, while a negative value does point to whipsaw markets.

mechanism: Same vertical NT buffers but applied prices are typical/median (vol-leaning); trend proxy = change in bar range; raise/lower stops only when range change aligns with positive NT-buffer correlation (ignore when corr≤0).
data_needed: High/low or typical/median price MAs; bar range series; NT buffers and Spearman corr; open positions for trailing.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDJPY daily context of Part 22; trailing class attached.
why_new_for_mis: Volatility-change trailing gated by MA-natural-transform coherence—MIS only trusts range expansion/contraction when multi-period MA spreads agree.
quote: decreases in the range would need to be backed by in positive correlations (values more than zero). The same would apply for increasing volatility.

mechanism: Horizontal composition: Cat1 price series → Cat2 dual MAs (functors A,C) → Cat3 DEMA-as-MA-of-MA (functors B,D); NT buffers AC and BD; Spearman corr>0 plus MA trend sign gates trailing stop moves (long only on uptrend+corr, short only on downtrend+corr); paired with Awesome Oscillator.
data_needed: Close prices; two MA periods; DEMA/MA-of-MA; m_transformations; correlation threshold (>0).
why_new_for_mis: Chained price→MA→smoothed-MA natural transforms whose mutual correlation becomes a regime confirmation for stop management—MIS multi-layer smoother-agreement sensor.
quote: a negative trend with a positive correlation between these buffers would be a green light to lower the stop loss on a short position.

mechanism: Same horizontal NT architecture but category-1 objects are bar ranges (high−low) instead of closes; Cat2 averages of ranges, Cat3 DEMA of range averages; NT correlation/trends then target volatility rather than price direction.
data_needed: High−low range series; MA/DEMA periods; NT buffers; optional trail or signal wiring.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD daily setup of Part 23 (proposed variant).
why_new_for_mis: Explicit range-series horizontal composition for volatility forecasting—MIS can reuse the NT stack on envelope width instead of price level.
quote: another approach we could have taken that horns more towards volatility would have been to have categorty-1 as a series of price ranges (highs minus lows).

mechanism: Rolling window of closes; log-spaced box sizes from min to max; CountBoxes = ceil((max−min)/(boxSize·Point)); regress log N(ε) vs log(1/ε); slope ≈ fractal dimension D; rising D → more jagged/chaotic structure, falling D → smoother regimes.
data_needed: Close buffer of InpDataLength; InpBoxSizesCount, InpMinBoxSize, InpMaxBoxSize; linear regression of log-log counts.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: General price chart indicator; chaos series context EURUSD H1 from Part 1.
why_new_for_mis: Scale-free jaggedness sensor of the price path—MIS chaos/complexity regime distinct from variance or ATR.
quote: A higher fractal dimension indicates a more complex, chaotic price structure, while a lower dimension may indicate smoother, predictable movement.

mechanism: Delay-embed closes (m, τ); within window mark pairs recurrent if Euclidean distance ≤ threshold·Point; RecurrenceRate = recurrent share; Determinism = share forming diagonal lines; Laminarity = share forming vertical lines—map stationary/deterministic/laminar vs random structure.
data_needed: Close series; InpEmbeddingDimension, InpTimeDelay, InpThreshold, InpWindowSize; pairwise distance matrix.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: General MT5 chart indicator; financial time-series recurrence analysis.
why_new_for_mis: Triplet of recurrence geometry measures as simultaneous mode sensors (trend/flat/chaos/predictability)—MIS nonlinear dynamics state beyond linear autocorr.
quote: Identify different market modes (trend, flat, chaotic state); Detect mode change; Assess the predictability of the market in different periods.

mechanism: Embed x(t)=[p(t),…,p(t+(m−1)τ)]; for current point find k nearest neighbors in lookback; forecast σ̂(t+h)=(1/k)Σ|return of neighbor over horizon h| from neighbors’ realized forward absolute returns (local density ↔ local volatility).
data_needed: Close series; m, τ, k, forecast horizon h, lookback; k-NN distances in embedding space.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Takens Volatility Forecast indicator on chart closes; EA tests EURUSD, AUD, GBPUSD from 2016.
why_new_for_mis: Phase-space local-density volatility sensor that borrows future abs-returns of geometric analogs—MIS nonlinear vol forecast without GARCH assumptions.
quote: This distance serves as a measure of local density and hence local volatility.

mechanism: Per bar: ACF first-lag under threshold → τ; FNN ratio under tolerance → m; reconstruct state; inverse-distance-weighted average of k neighbors’ prices at +horizon → prediction; trade long if pred>close else short; optional dynamic lot from chaotic vol.
data_needed: Close history InpLookback; ACF maxLag; FNN maxDim/threshold/tolerance; k neighbors; forecast horizon.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD, AUD pair, GBPUSD; tests from 2016-01-01; chart timeframe of attached symbol.
why_new_for_mis: Self-tuning embedding (ACF+FNN) plus analog forecasting as an online chaos-state sensor for directional bias—MIS adaptive phase-space predictor, not fixed-lag regression.
quote: we find the states of the system in the past that are closest to the current state. Based on their future behavior, we make a forecast for the current state.

mechanism: Argue linear orders must drop long-legged/gravestone/dragonfly Doji as incomparable bull/bear labels; partial orders keep them via antisymmetry/undefined slots so support-resistance Doji regions remain in the ordered decision set for exits.
data_needed: OHLC candle classification; partial-order binary relation allowing undefined pairs; trailing decision monoids.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDJPY trailing case study; candle-pattern illustration general.
why_new_for_mis: Sensing policy that refuses to force-label indecision candles—MIS can retain S/R-critical Doji states instead of omitting them under total orders.
quote: long legged Doji candles, and other candles like it which include Gravestone Doji and the Dragonfly Doji, tend to feature in major price support and resistance regions.
